pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/review/page-05.png with Read and looked at it. Top wide panel: the doctor gestures toward Ravi, who is seated. Her balloon at top centre-right reads 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' The tail points to the doctor. A teal label at left over the laptop reads 'PATIENT DETAILS: current vitals · prior health info · allergy panel · AI mic option · patient docs · lab reports'. Middle wide panel, long shot: doctor at left, laptop with a mic and shield icon in the centre, Ravi at right. The doctor's balloon reads 'May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?'. Ravi's balloon reads 'Yes, I agree.' Its long tail runs diagonally down to him. A teal label at right reads 'AI VOICE CONSENT: asked at the first visit, before any voice is saved'. Bottom-left panel: Ravi rubs his neck. Balloon: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' The tail points to him. A teal label at bottom left reads 'SOAP NOTES: fill in manually and choose ICD or SNOMED codes, or let AI listen and summarise the conversation', with a glowing mic icon on a laptop beside it. Bottom-right panel: caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The doctor listens with a soft smile, and Ravi is seen from behind in the foreground.
pages.observation: Reading works: greeting, consent question, consent, consent label, symptom, closing caption. In the top panel the large PATIENT DETAILS label at left starts below the balloon, but because it is on the left a reader may glance at it before the greeting. The balloon is higher, so most readers will still read it first. Mild ambiguity. In the middle panel the question and 'Yes, I agree.' balloons sit edge to edge with almost no gap. They read in the correct order, but they look joined. 'talk?' touches or nearly touches its balloon's right border. The PATIENT DETAILS label covers most of the laptop on the desk. The SOAP NOTES label covers the left part of the laptop, and its last line ends close to the box edge. The consent label has no final period. Ravi's tail tip in the bottom-left panel ends at his ear and hair, and the doctor's top-panel tail ends near her mouth. Neither covers a face. Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' gets no spoken reply on this page. The caption and the listening doctor carry it, and her reply comes on page 6. This is acceptable, but the link only appears after the page turn. The page is dense with interface text, but all of it is legible.
